clue.text: See 19
Schmuck wearing jacket

parts.note: schmuck is Yiddish-derived slang for a fool, a jerk
someone wearing a coat is in it, so wearing gives IN

explanation.surface: A fool has put on a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' reads as a verb linking fool and jacket, but it supplies a word of its own, IN, as in 'in a suit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, historically of leather.

clue.text: Invention of Edison taken from a 90° angle

indicators.note: an invention is something made up, so the letters of the inventor's name are made into something new

explanation.surface: A gadget of Thomas Edison's photographed from a right angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invention of Edison' looks like a reference to the phonograph or bulb; instead the six letters of EDISON are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewed or photographed at right angles to the front, that is, from the side.

clue.text: One child has no involvement with another for the most part — that's the truth!

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a kid is a child

indicators.note: NO is involved with, that is enclosed in, the next piece
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: another child, a youth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child refuses to play with another one, and that's the honest truth!
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims the last letter; 'has ... involvement with' puts NO inside the result. 'another' means another child.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal exclamation insisting that what has just been said is true, not a joke.

clue.text: Muse with sovereign detailing something elementary

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: de-tailing: cutting off the tail, the last letter

parts.note: an atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element

explanation.surface: A muse goes with the monarch, explaining something basic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailing' looks like 'explaining in detail' but means removing the tail, so ATOM becomes ATO. ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Time put in to succeed with delivery in football

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time is placed inside the following letters

parts.note: taken as written
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
to succeed is to win

explanation.surface: Extra minutes are added so a side can win a football match with one more delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' here is the abbreviation for hour, not the usual T, and 'put in' places it inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a throw-in restarts play by hurling the ball from the touchline with both hands.

clue.text: Broadcast protects English line on important document

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered, like seed sown widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcaster safeguards an English stance on a key document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' scatters PROTECTS plus E (English).
explanation.definitionFit: A classification stamped or printed across the top of a highly confidential paper.

clue.text: Opener gives call before cricket shot

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a pull is a cricket stroke hitting a short ball to the leg side

explanation.surface: Someone telephones before a cricket stroke is played.
explanation.walkthrough: A PULL is a cricket stroke played across the line to leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring pull is the tab that opens a drinks can, so it is a can opener of sorts.

clue.text: Cake's half hidden by tarts — it's not important

indicators.note: the half-cake goes inside the word for tarts, covered by it

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute, a whore

indicators.note: the first half of the word cake

explanation.surface: Half a cake vanishes beneath some pastries, but nobody minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tarts' suggests pastries beside the cake but is slang for prostitutes; 'hidden by' puts half of CAKE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Who cares? is an idiomatic shrug meaning the matter is of no consequence.

clue.text: A number of points about love's absurdity

indicators.note: the run of points goes around the letter for love

parts.note: a string of compass points: N, N, S, E, N, S, E
love is nil, O, in tennis scores

explanation.surface: Several aspects of love are ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points, seven of them strung together around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is foolish, meaningless talk or behaviour, a synonym of absurdity.

clue.text: 6's 2 across

parts.note: 6 is the ring, read as a circle; two of its centre-to-edge lines laid end to end span it from side to side

explanation.walkthrough: The 6 refers to the first half of 6/21, a ring, read here as a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Two radii of a circle laid end to end along a line make its diameter, going right across.

clue.text: Instrument planner used round the house

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for house
used in the sense of worn or abused, so the letters are knocked into a new form

explanation.surface: A planner makes use of an instrument around the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges PLANNER into ALPENRN, which goes 'round' HO, the abbreviation for house.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenhorn is a very long wooden horn played by Alpine herdsmen.

clue.text: Key to the Guardian solver's ultimate escape from reality here?

parts.note: piano keys are traditionally made of ivory
taken as written
a newspaper speaks of itself in editorials as we

indicators.note: the last letter of the word solver

explanation.surface: The secret of the Guardian solver is escaping from the real world.
explanation.walkthrough: A newspaper's editorial voice is 'we', so the Guardian gives WE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a place of privileged seclusion, cut off from the practicalities of real life.

clue.text: See 24
German emperor, perfect European to stop massacre

indicators.note: the inner pieces stop up, plugging, the word for massacre

parts.note: to massacre is to kill
A1, written AI, means first-rate
a Serb is a European from Serbia

explanation.surface: A German emperor sends a flawless European to halt a slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 for perfect is written with the letter I standing in for the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser Bill was the British nickname for Wilhelm II, German emperor during the First World War.

clue.text: Dangerous motorway drivers — where they don't want to end up

definitions.meaning: drivers who overtake on the wrong, inside lane

definitions.text: where they don't want to end up
definitions.meaning: such reckless drivers do not want to land with the funeral directors

explanation.surface: Reckless drivers on the motorway risk ending up somewhere they'd rather not.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang undertaking is passing another car on the inside lane, a dangerous manoeuvre; the second sense is funeral directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: drivers who pass on the inside, and funeral directors who handle the dead.

clue.text: German article, doppelgänger's gun

parts.note: der is the masculine German word for 'the'
a ringer, or dead ringer, is someone's double

explanation.surface: A German piece of writing about someone's double and his gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is the grammatical word for 'the', not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small short-barrelled pocket pistol, named after Henry Deringer.

clue.text: Cuts immediately

definitions.meaning: chops, said twice, as in cutting with blows
an informal call for speed: quickly, at once

explanation.definitionFit: Chop is to cut with blows, doubled; chop-chop is pidgin-derived slang urging haste.

clue.text: A game starts to get interesting attacking defence

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A game begins to get interesting when the attack is on the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence' sounds like the sporting side being attacked; here it means a written justification.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's beliefs or conduct.

clue.text: The medicine man's beastly carriers?

parts.note: beastly read literally, of a beast: here the beast is a hippopotamus, short form hippo
crates are containers for carrying goods

explanation.surface: A doctor's boxes for transporting animals?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the name as two words: carriers for a beast, hippo crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek physician called the father of medicine.

clue.text: He shot his wife, He's serving life!

definitions.text: He shot his wife, He's serving life!

parts.words: He shot his wife, He's serving life!
parts.note: a rhyming couplet in which a crime is followed by a fitting punishment, delivered in verse

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is itself a rhyme, so the deserved punishment is poetic in two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic justice is an outcome in which wrongdoing is punished in a fitting way.

clue.text: In such a calendar one door's opening, then another opening

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word door

parts.note: a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out

explanation.surface: Each day of this calendar a door opens, then another one does.
explanation.walkthrough: Advent calendars have a little door to open for each December day before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent calendar counts down the days of Advent, the season before Christmas.

clue.text: See 6
Nibbles bit of fish, fresh, 40% off, knocked back with tasty skin?

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish

indicators.note: the word for tasty forms a skin wrapping round the inner letters

parts.note: tasty food is good

indicators.note: knocked back as in reversed, so the letters run the other way
two of the five letters, 40 per cent, come off the end, keeping the first three

explanation.surface: Snacks of fish, fresh and discounted, washed down with something nicely crisp-skinned.
explanation.walkthrough: '40% off' leaves FRE, which 'knocked back' turns to ERF; 'skin' wraps the word for tasty around it. 'Nibbles' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Finger food means small snacks eaten by hand, such as party nibbles.

clue.text: Write, for instance, "to rise" as your answer?

definitions.text: Write, for instance, "to rise" as your answer?

parts.words: Write, for instance, "to rise" as your answer?
parts.note: a phrase meaning to stand or rise, offered as the solution for this down light

explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites you to supply the everyday phrasal verb meaning 'to rise' as your entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To get up is to rise from bed or a seat; as a noun it also means an outfit.

clue.text: Equestrian event boring people

parts.note: flat means dull, lacking interest
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A horse show tires the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' means dull, not drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat race is a horse race run without jumps.

clue.text: The Sun's hottest part?

parts.note: read either as the tabloid's best bit or the brightest, most elevated light in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, so its hottest part is its best bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A highlight is the most outstanding or enjoyable part of something.

clue.text: Fibre among Marxist-Leninists

indicators.note: the answer is found among the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Moral fibre found among communist revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the hyphen in MarxIST-LEninists.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong plant fibre from agave or yucca, used for cords and brushes.

clue.text: Stapler ruined holy book

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A stapler has damaged a sacred book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' signals the rearrangement of STAPLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a book containing the Psalms, used in worship.

clue.text: Entering stakes, card left over proves a stinker

indicators.note: the reversed letters go into the word for stakes

parts.note: the pot is the pool of stakes in a card game

indicators.note: over as in turned over, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Joining a poker game, a card left over turns out to be a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card left' gives ACE + L; 'over' turns it to LECA, 'Entering' POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A polecat is a weasel-like animal notorious for its foul-smelling secretions.
